messages: wet-basement-repair	Stop basement leaks and protect your home's foundation with our permanent waterproofing solutions, guaranteed for 20 years.	A damp basement signals more than just a minor annoyance; it often points to deeper structural vulnerabilities. Our process begins with a meticulous inspection, employing advanced diagnostic tools to pinpoint the exact entry points and pathways of water. We don't just patch visible leaks; we uncover the hidden issues compromising your home's integrity.

Whether it's interior drainage systems, exterior excavation for weeping tile replacement, or precision crack injections, we tailor our approach. We install robust sump pumps with battery backups to manage heavy water flow, ensuring your basement remains dry even during severe storms. Our solutions are engineered for long-term effectiveness, not temporary fixes.

Imagine a basement transformed from a damp, musty space into a dry, usable area, free from mold and structural concerns. You gain peace of mind knowing your foundation is secure and your indoor air quality is protected. Our 20-year warranty underscores our commitment to a permanently dry and healthy home environment.	[{"title":"Subsurface Drainage Renewal","desc":"We excavate and replace compromised weeping tiles, redirecting groundwater away from your foundation before it can penetrate your basement walls."},{"title":"Reliable Water Ejection","desc":"High-capacity sump pumps, often with battery backups, actively remove accumulated water, preventing hydrostatic pressure buildup and flooding."},{"title":"Foundation Preservation","desc":"By eliminating water intrusion, we halt the erosion and deterioration of your concrete foundation, safeguarding your home's structural stability."},{"title":"Improved Indoor Air Quality","desc":"A dry basement prevents mold and mildew growth, significantly enhancing your home's air quality and creating a healthier living environment."}]	[{"q":"How do I know if my basement has a water problem or just condensation?","a":"Condensation forms on cold surfaces like pipes and walls when warm humid air hits them. You can test the difference by taping a piece of plastic sheeting to the wall and sealing the edges. If moisture appears on the room side of the plastic after a day or two, it is condensation. If moisture appears on the wall side, water is coming through the foundation. Most wet basements in London Ontario involve actual water intrusion, not just condensation."},{"q":"What causes wet basements in London Ontario specifically?","a":"London sits on clay-heavy soil that expands when wet and contracts when dry. This movement puts pressure on foundation walls over time, causing cracks. Many homes in older London neighbourhoods like Old North, Byron, and Old South were built before modern waterproofing standards, and their drainage systems are aging. Spring snowmelt and heavy rainfall events are the most common triggers for basement flooding in this area."},{"q":"Is a wet basement covered by home insurance in Ontario?","a":"It depends on the cause. Sudden and accidental water damage from a burst pipe or a one-time sewer backup is usually covered. Gradual seepage through foundation cracks or chronic drainage problems is typically excluded as a maintenance issue. If you have overland flood coverage or sewer backup coverage as add-ons to your policy, those may apply. Always check your specific policy and call your insurer before doing repairs."},{"q":"What is the difference between interior and exterior waterproofing?","a":"Exterior waterproofing involves excavating around the foundation, applying a waterproof membrane to the outside of the wall, and installing new drainage tile. It addresses the problem at the source but is more disruptive and expensive. Interior waterproofing involves installing a drainage channel along the interior perimeter of the basement floor, directing water to a sump pump. It does not stop water from entering the wall but manages it before it reaches the floor. Both approaches are legitimate depending on the situation."},{"q":"How long does a wet basement repair take?","a":"Most interior waterproofing jobs in a typical London home take one to two days. Exterior waterproofing that requires excavation can take three to five days depending on the size of the foundation and site access. Crack injection repairs are usually completed in a few hours. We will give you a clear timeline before work begins."},{"q":"What is the 20-year warranty on wet basement repairs?","a":"Our wet basement waterproofing work is backed by a written 20-year warranty. If the repaired area develops a water problem within that period, we come back and fix it at no charge. The warranty is transferable to new owners if you sell the home, which can be a selling point."},{"q":"Can tree roots cause a wet basement?","a":"Yes. Tree roots can crack foundation walls and drainage tile over time. They can also block the weeping tile around your foundation, preventing proper drainage and causing water to build up against the wall. If you have large trees close to your house, root intrusion is worth investigating as part of any basement water assessment."},{"q":"Should I use a sump pump or waterproofing, or both?","a":"A sump pump removes water that has already entered the drainage system. Waterproofing prevents or manages water before it reaches the living space. In many cases, both are used together. The sump pump handles the water collected by the interior drainage channel, and the waterproofing membrane or crack repairs reduce the amount of water getting in. We assess each situation individually and recommend what is actually needed."},{"q":"How much does wet basement repair cost in Ontario?","a":"Costs vary significantly depending on the method and the size of the problem. Crack injection repairs typically range from a few hundred to around a thousand dollars per crack. Interior drainage systems for a full basement can range from several thousand to over ten thousand dollars. Exterior excavation and waterproofing is generally the most expensive option. We provide written quotes before any work begins so there are no surprises."},{"q":"What is weeping tile and does my house have it?","a":"Weeping tile is a perforated pipe installed around the perimeter of a foundation to collect groundwater and direct it away from the house. Most homes built in London after the 1950s have some form of weeping tile, though older systems used clay tile that can crack, collapse, or become blocked with roots over time. A camera inspection can determine whether your weeping tile is functioning properly."},{"q":"Can I waterproof a basement myself?","a":"Some minor crack repairs can be done with hydraulic cement or epoxy injection kits available at hardware stores. However, these are surface fixes and may not address the underlying cause. For persistent or widespread water problems, professional assessment is recommended. Improper repairs can mask the problem temporarily while allowing damage to continue behind the walls."},{"q":"Does a wet basement affect the structural integrity of my home?","a":"Over time, yes. Water that repeatedly saturates the soil around a foundation can cause settling and movement. Chronic moisture weakens mortar joints in block foundations and can cause bowing or cracking in poured concrete walls. If you are seeing horizontal cracks in a block foundation wall, that is a structural concern that should be assessed promptly."},{"q":"What should I do immediately if my basement floods?","a":"First, make sure it is safe to enter. If there is any possibility of electrical hazards, stay out and call an electrician or emergency services. Once it is safe, remove standing water as quickly as possible using a wet-dry vacuum or pump. Move belongings to dry areas and start fans and dehumidifiers to prevent mould. Document the damage with photos for insurance purposes. Then call us to assess the source of the problem so it does not happen again."}]	Wet Basement Repair London ON | 20-Year Warranty | Discount Drain	Permanent wet basement waterproofing in London Ontario with a 20-year warranty. Emergency service available 24/7. Call Discount Drain: 519-451-8342.

trenchless-pipe-repair	Repair your pipes without digging, restoring flow and integrity with minimal disruption.	Our Cured-In-Place Pipe (CIPP) lining system creates a new, robust pipe directly within your existing damaged one. We insert a resin-saturated felt tube, then inflate and cure it, forming a seamless, jointless replacement. This advanced method ensures a complete structural repair without disturbing your property.

Imagine restoring your home's essential drainage without the chaos of trenches across your lawn or driveway. You avoid the significant costs and inconvenience of landscape restoration, concrete repairs, or asphalt patching. Your daily routine remains largely uninterrupted, as most trenchless repairs are completed efficiently, often within a single day.

This innovative solution specifically targets common issues like root intrusion, cracks, and corrosion by creating a pipe stronger than the original. It prevents future leaks and blockages, offering a long-term fix that traditional dig-and-replace methods often cannot match in terms of speed and minimal impact.	[{"title":"No Property Damage","desc":"Your landscaping, driveway, and yard remain completely intact, avoiding costly and time-consuming restoration work."},{"title":"Superior Pipe Strength","desc":"The new CIPP liner is seamless, jointless, and more resistant to root intrusion and corrosion than conventional pipes."},{"title":"Rapid Completion","desc":"Most trenchless pipe repairs are finished within a single day, minimizing disruption to your home or business operations."},{"title":"Long-Term Reliability","desc":"Enjoy a durable, structurally sound pipe system designed to last for decades, preventing recurring issues and future repairs."}]	[{"q":"What is trenchless pipe repair and how does it work?","a":"Trenchless pipe repair replaces or rehabilitates a damaged underground pipe without digging a trench along its length. The two main methods are pipe lining (CIPP), where a resin-coated liner is inserted and cured inside the existing pipe to form a new one, and pipe bursting, where a head is pulled through the old pipe to break it outward while pulling new pipe in behind it. Both methods require only small access points at each end."},{"q":"Is trenchless pipe repair available in London Ontario?","a":"Yes. Discount Drain has been performing trenchless repairs in London and Southwestern Ontario for years. We use CIPP lining and pipe bursting depending on the condition of the pipe and the specific situation."},{"q":"How much does trenchless pipe repair cost in Ontario?","a":"For a typical residential sewer line in London, pipe lining generally runs between $4,000 and $8,000 depending on the length, depth, and condition of the pipe. This is significantly less than traditional excavation, which can run $10,000 to $20,000 or more once driveway restoration is included. A camera inspection is needed to give you an accurate quote."},{"q":"Is trenchless repair as durable as replacing the pipe?","a":"Yes. A properly installed CIPP liner creates a seamless pipe inside the existing one, with no joints for roots to enter. The liner material is rated for 50 years or more under normal conditions. In many cases, the lined pipe outperforms a new clay tile or cast iron pipe because the smooth interior improves flow."},{"q":"Can trenchless repair be done under a driveway or landscaping?","a":"That is one of the main advantages. Because no trench is needed, the driveway, garden, patio, or lawn above the pipe is left completely undisturbed. This is why trenchless repair often costs less overall even if the per-foot cost of the liner is similar to new pipe, because there is no restoration work afterward."},{"q":"What pipe materials can be repaired with trenchless methods?","a":"CIPP lining works in clay tile, cast iron, concrete, and PVC pipe. Pipe bursting is typically used for clay tile and cast iron. The condition and diameter of the existing pipe determines which method is appropriate. A camera inspection will show us what we are working with."},{"q":"How long does trenchless pipe repair take?","a":"Most residential trenchless repairs are completed in a single day. The liner curing process takes a few hours depending on the method used (heat or UV). You will typically have your drains back in service by the end of the day."},{"q":"Can trenchless repair fix root intrusion?","a":"Yes. If roots have entered the pipe through cracks or joint gaps, lining the pipe seals those entry points permanently. The liner creates a smooth, continuous surface with no joints, which eliminates the gaps that roots exploit. Roots already inside the pipe are cleared before the liner is installed."},{"q":"What happens if the pipe is too damaged for trenchless repair?","a":"If the pipe has collapsed completely or the structural damage is too severe for lining to adhere properly, pipe bursting may still be an option. If neither trenchless method is viable, we will tell you honestly and explain what excavation would involve. We do not push trenchless repair when it is not the right solution."},{"q":"Does trenchless repair require a permit in Ontario?","a":"Permit requirements vary by municipality. In London, some sewer repair work requires a permit from the city. We handle the permit process as part of the job so you do not have to navigate that on your own."},{"q":"Will trenchless repair fix a bellied pipe?","a":"A bellied pipe is a section that has sagged and holds standing water. Lining a bellied pipe does not fix the sag, but it can seal cracks and prevent further deterioration. In some cases, the belly is minor enough that lining is still worthwhile. In others, excavation to correct the grade is the better option. The camera footage will show us the severity."},{"q":"Is trenchless pipe repair covered by home insurance in Ontario?","a":"Some Ontario home insurance policies include sewer backup or water damage coverage that may apply to sewer line repair. Coverage varies significantly by policy and insurer. We recommend calling your broker before the repair to understand what is covered. We can work with your insurance company directly if needed."},{"q":"How do I know if my pipe is a candidate for trenchless repair?","a":"A camera inspection is the only way to know for certain. The camera shows us the condition of the pipe, the location and type of damage, and whether the pipe has enough structural integrity to support a liner. We will give you a clear answer after the inspection."}]	Trenchless Pipe Repair London ON | No-Dig Sewer Repair | Discount Drain	Trenchless sewer pipe repair in London Ontario. No digging, no driveway damage. CIPP lining replaces your pipe in one day. Call Discount Drain: 519-451-8342.

sewer-repair-installation	Restore your sewer's flow and foundation with expert repair and precise new installations.	When your sewer line shows signs of trouble—slow drains, foul odors, or sudden backups—you need immediate, decisive action. We pinpoint the exact issue, whether it's a collapsed pipe, root intrusion, or aging infrastructure, ensuring a lasting fix. Our approach addresses the root cause, preventing recurring problems and protecting your property from further damage.

For complex repairs or new installations, our specialized fleet, including excavators and combination vac trucks, handles the toughest jobs. These machines efficiently expose damaged lines, clear debris, and prepare the site for new pipe laying, minimizing disruption to your property. We ensure every component meets rigorous standards.

We manage all necessary permits and coordinate directly with the City of London and surrounding municipalities on your behalf. This meticulous process guarantees your sewer repair or installation complies with all Ontario Building Code requirements, providing you with complete peace of mind and a fully functional, reliable sewer system.	[{"title":"Precise Problem Identification","desc":"We use advanced camera inspections to accurately locate and diagnose sewer line issues, avoiding unnecessary excavation and costs."},{"title":"Specialized Equipment Deployment","desc":"Our fleet of excavators and vac trucks efficiently handles trenching, debris removal, and pipe placement for durable repairs and installations."},{"title":"Full Permit and City Coordination","desc":"We manage all municipal permits and liaise with local authorities, ensuring your project meets all regulatory standards without hassle."},{"title":"Long-Term System Reliability","desc":"By addressing root causes and installing high-grade materials, your new or repaired sewer system delivers lasting performance and prevents future disruptions."}]	[{"q":"How much does sewer line repair cost in London Ontario?","a":"Costs vary significantly depending on the method used and the extent of the damage. Trenchless pipe lining for a typical residential line runs $4,000 to $8,000. Full excavation and replacement can run $10,000 to $20,000 or more once driveway restoration is included. A camera inspection is the only way to give you an accurate number for your specific situation."},{"q":"How do I know if my sewer line needs to be repaired or replaced?","a":"A sewer camera inspection is the definitive answer. Signs that suggest a problem include multiple slow drains, gurgling toilets, sewage smell inside the house, sewage backing up into the basement floor drain, and soggy patches in the yard. The camera shows us exactly what is happening and where, so we can recommend the right solution."},{"q":"What type of sewer pipe is in my older London Ontario home?","a":"Most homes built before the 1980s in London have clay tile sewer lines. Clay tile was the standard material for decades and can last a long time, but it is susceptible to root intrusion, cracking from ground movement, and joint separation over time. Homes built in the 1980s and later typically have PVC or ABS pipe, which is more resistant to roots and corrosion."},{"q":"Who is responsible for the sewer line from my house to the street?","a":"The sewer line has two sections. The private section from your house to the property line is your responsibility. The Private Drain Connection (PDC) from the property line to the city main is also technically your responsibility to maintain, but the City of London offers a flat-rate PDC renewal program. As of 2026, the fee is $7,250 and can be paid over 10 years through your property taxes. A camera inspection can determine which section has the problem."},{"q":"Can the city be responsible for any part of my sewer repair?","a":"The City of London's PDC renewal program covers the section of the line from your property line to the city main at a flat rate of $7,250 as of 2026. This can be added to your property taxes over 10 years. If the camera shows the main problem is in the city's portion of the line, this program is worth knowing about before agreeing to private repair work."},{"q":"What is the difference between sewer repair and sewer replacement?","a":"Repair addresses specific damaged sections of the pipe, either through trenchless lining, spot excavation and patching, or pipe bursting. Replacement involves removing and replacing the entire line, usually through full excavation. The right approach depends on the extent and location of the damage. We will recommend the most cost-effective solution after the camera inspection."},{"q":"How long does sewer line repair take?","a":"Trenchless repairs are typically completed in a single day. Excavation and replacement takes longer, usually two to five days depending on the length of the line, the depth, and the surface restoration required. We will give you a clear timeline before starting."},{"q":"Will sewer repair require a permit in London Ontario?","a":"Yes, most sewer repair work in London requires a permit from the city. We handle the permit process as part of the job."},{"q":"Can sewer repair be done in winter in Ontario?","a":"Yes, though frozen ground can complicate excavation work. Trenchless repairs are generally not affected by cold weather. If you have an emergency in winter, call us and we will assess what is possible given the conditions."},{"q":"What happens to my yard or driveway during sewer repair?","a":"With trenchless methods, the surface above the pipe is left undisturbed. With excavation, the area above the trench needs to be restored after the pipe is repaired. We restore the surface as part of the job, though concrete driveways may require a separate concrete contractor depending on the scope."},{"q":"Is sewer line repair covered by home insurance in Ontario?","a":"Some Ontario home insurance policies include sewer backup or water damage coverage that may apply to sewer line repair. Coverage varies significantly by policy and insurer. We recommend calling your broker before the repair to understand what is covered. We can work with your insurance company directly if needed."},{"q":"What is a sewer liner and how long does it last?","a":"A sewer liner (CIPP) is a resin-coated tube that is inserted into the existing pipe and cured in place to form a new pipe inside the old one. A properly installed liner is rated for 50 years or more. It creates a seamless, smooth interior with no joints for roots to enter, which often improves flow compared to the original pipe."},{"q":"Can I get a second opinion on a sewer repair quote?","a":"Absolutely. If you have been quoted for sewer repair and want a second assessment, call us at 519-451-8342. We include a free camera inspection with every service call, so you will see exactly what we see and can compare assessments directly."}]	Sewer Repair and Installation London ON | Discount Drain	Professional sewer repair and installation in London and Southwestern Ontario. Certified technicians, full fleet, all permits handled. Call 519-451-8342.
